author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sebastien grew up believing chivalry made him a “good man”, until feminist thinkers revealed hidden layers of benevolent sexism. Through a striking personal story, he invites men to rethink the way they move through the world. What if modern chivalry wasn’t about opening doors, but opening safer spaces? Entrepreneur and activist, Sebastien bridges corporate experience and entrepreneurial spirit to promote gender equality and inclusion. After years in major companies, he founded Men at Work to turn men into agents of change within organizations. His activism drives one conviction: gender equality will only happen when men step up. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Chivalry is outdated. Here's what to do instead. | Sebastien Garcin | TEDxLuxembourgCityWomen

author: TEDx Talks
description: As Chief Investment Officer of the New York City Pension Fund, Seema Hingorani kept hearing the same excuse for why there were so few women managing money – “we just don’t get resumes from women.” So she made a deal with the industry: “I will find them, if you hire them.” In this talk, she shares how that challenge seeded Girls Who Invest, a program which has brought more than 4,000 college women into investing in the past decade, and why women need to control far more of the world’s capital.  Seema Hingorani is the Founder and Chair of Girls Who Invest, a non-profit organization focused on increasing the number of women in the asset management industry. Her career is characterized by deep expertise in investment management coupled with a longstanding passion to advance gender equity in finance. She previously served as Chief Investment Officer of the New York City Retirement Systems and held senior leadership roles at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, including Managing Director,
title: Where are all the women investors? | Seema Hingorani | TEDxPenn

In her talk, she will share about how translanguaging practices may unlock the full linguistic power of multilingual speakers, turning linguistic diversity from a perceived deficit into a profound strength for equity and innovation. Through years of work in housing and urban policy, she’s seen how planning decisions quietly shape what gets built, where homes are allowed, and who can afford to live in them. What most people don’t realise is that today’s housing system rests on historical foundations. At TEDxUQ 2026, Rachel explores the deeper history behind Australia’s housing crisis and argues that understanding how our system was built is essential if we want to build enough homes now. An urban planner and researcher, Rachel Gallagher is passionate about one big question: who are our cities really built for? Through years of work in housing and urban policy, she’s seen how planning decisions quietly shape our daily lives—where we can live, how we move, and who benefits from growth. She shows us how breathwork became her anchor through stress, expectation and self-doubt, and how this simple, powerful tool can help all of us move from survival mode into calm, clarity and confident action. Today, she invites us to breathe like an Olympian. Anna-Liza is a speaker, a breathwork expert and an Olympian. description: Allanah is a Kurnu-Barkindji and Malyangapa writer, editor and academic. She is interested in social justice, mental health, Blak feminism, First Nations storytelling, queer identities and she is now writing about her disease of endometriosis. In her PhD, she explored affective learning, ownership of women’s bodies and Unremarked Whiteness, inserting an original Indigenous female superhero into the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Her first book, Forever and Ever, has just been released and she had her book launch recently. At TEDxUQ 2026, Allanah shares about the power of language and why cultural sensitivity readers are about educating people on marginalised cultures and not censorship. description:
L'innovation ne dépend pas de l'endroit où l'on se trouve, mais de notre capacité à créer des connexions, à rester ouverts et à transformer les singularités d'un territoire en opportunités.
L'innovation est souvent associée aux grandes métropoles, aux pôles technologiques et aux écosystèmes mondialement reconnus. Pourtant, certaines des entreprises les plus ambitieuses naissent loin des centres de décision.
À travers son parcours entre le Pays basque, la Suède et le développement international d'Adaxis, Henri Bernard montre comment un territoire, lorsqu'il cultive son identité tout en restant ouvert sur le monde, peut devenir un formidable accélérateur d'innovation.
Son témoignage interroge notre manière de penser l'entrepreneuriat, l'attractivité des territoires et les conditions qui favorisent l'émergence des idées. title: Faut-il partir pour réussir ? | Henri Bernard | TEDxESTIA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Le futur ne se construit pas pour les citoyens. Il se construit avec eux.
Plusieurs décisions prises aujourd’hui façonneront la vie de millions de personnes pendant plusieurs décennies. L'intelligence artificielle, l'éducation, le travail, la recherche, la santé, le climat, la démocratie... Pourtant, les espaces où ces décisions se construisent réunissent presque toujours les mêmes profils : gouvernements, entreprises, experts, chercheurs. Les citoyens directement concernés et plus encore les jeunes, qui vivront le plus longtemps avec ces choix, restent souvent absents de ces conversations. À travers son parcours, des Comores à Inria, en passant par l'ESTIA et plusieurs projets internationaux en Europe et en Afrique, Chelza Inzouddine partage une conviction née du terrain : les meilleures décisions ne sont pas seulement celles prises pour les citoyens, mais celles construites avec eux.

title: Arrêtons de construire le futur sans ceux qui devront y vivre | Chelza Inzouddine | TEDxESTIA

description: As the world changes faster than ever, preparing for the future may require more than developing new skills. Jimmy Naraine explores the inner qualities that help us navigate uncertainty, disruption and change. His talk challenges us to consider whether our greatest preparation for the future begins within ourselves. Jimmy Naraine es educador global y speaker internacional que ha impactado a cientos de miles de personas en el mundo. Su trabajo combina ciencia, experiencia personal y acción para abordar cómo adaptarnos a un futuro que avanza más rápido que nuestra biología. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if some of our biggest decisions were never really about what we thought they were? Sudeep Chawla suggests that childhood experiences leave us with quiet questions, such as 'Am I enough?', 'Do I matter?' or 'Will people leave me?', which we then spend years trying to answer through our careers, relationships and achievements. Drawing on a lifelong pursuit of approval and a personal loss that no achievement could fix, he introduces a practice he calls question spotting and offers three ways to stop letting an old question choose the course of our lives. With leadership stints at Sintex, Pidilite, and Mondelēz, Sudeep has spent years building brands that millions of consumers know and trust. Beyond scaling iconic market leaders, he shapes the industry's future through his popular podcast by combining raw consumer insights with purpose-driven strategy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at

La véritable performance ne consiste pas à aller plus vite que les autres. Elle consiste à avancer ensemble, sans laisser personne derrière.
Dans nos entreprises, dans le sport comme dans la société, nous associons souvent la performance à la vitesse, à la compétition et aux résultats. Mais que vaut une victoire si certains restent sur le bord du chemin ?

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the music in our playlist could do more than entertain us? In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Gauri Yadwadkar explores the therapeutic potential of Indian Raag music and its connection with the human mind and body. Drawing from the ancient traditions of Indian classical music and emerging neuroscience research, she examines how specific raags may influence attention, emotional regulation, stress, and overall wellbeing.

From Raga Darbari and Jogiya to the ancient sound of Aum, the talk brings together tradition and modern science to ask a simple question: What if, instead of asking what music we like, we asked what music our brain needs today?

The talk offers a perspective on music not as a replacement for medicine, but as a potential companion to healthcare, self-care, and emotional wellbeing. Perhaps the most powerful medicine we carry every day isn’t in our pocket. It’s in our playlist. Head of Content / A&R (Non-Film) at Times Music, the label under Bennett, Coleman & C
title: Power of Indian Raag Music to deal and heal | Ms. Gauri Yadwadkar | TEDxIIHMR U

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The speaker begins with the history of cross-casting, the practice of having actors play characters whose identities differ from their own. By examining this practice, she explores how identity labels can be challenged and how identity itself can be fluid. Finally, she discusses the significance of cross-casting and invites the audience to experience it for themselves in the theater.
 嗨大家好，我是Aurora徐婧，一枚热衷于中国传统文化和马术障碍的剧女。我与戏剧的缘分从中国舞开始，渐渐延伸至台前幕后的每一寸空间。初中创办汉服社、举办校中国文化周，曾穿着汉服站上过秀场舞台，也曾在辩席间获得中文辩论赛“最佳辩手”。这些肢体和语言的经历让我体会到表达的重量。高中后我逐渐转向幕后，是小黑屋常客—负责高中部每一场演出的灯光控制，也是学校energy club现役负责人。从小黑屋的位置看去，舞台是另一番模样。而真正让我沉溺的，是剧场里不可复制的瞬间。从《永不消逝的电波》的雨夜谍影，到《只此青绿》的千里江山；从《红楼梦》葬花的漫天飞花，到《十面埋伏》刀光剑影的垓下悲歌；从舞台布局的华美绮梦，到一桌二椅的简约克制…我流连于不同的文化语汇之间，逐渐领悟到：同一段旋律、同一个主题，在不同社会文化的土壤里，能绽放截然不同的花朵。 这也让我开始对心理与性别研究产生兴趣——人生如戏，舞台从来不只是舞台，而是社会潜意识最诚实的写照。课余时间，我喜欢用文字打捞那些稍纵即逝的感受——写过校刊，也写剧评repo。剧场里和文学作品里那种周而复始的、静默的、却蕴含全部生命力的表达方式，也贯穿了我一些不成章法的创作。马术、舞蹈、文学，是我理解世界的方式；从肢体到语言，我在其中摸索着与世界接触的钥匙。初中时常看TED演讲，从没想到有一天自己会站在这个平台上。我的兴趣或许不够主流，但正因如此，我格外渴望在这里遇见同频的各位小
title: 她扮作他：EGO，不止一种模样 | Aurora Xu | TEDxSSBS Youth

description: The speaker shares an experience of confronting her ego during a conflict with a team member, and she comes to the conclusion that ego is not the enemy; unchecked ego is. 我就读于星河湾双语学校，即将升入六年级。我一直对演讲和辩论充满兴趣，喜欢在表达中梳理自己的想法，也很享受和他人交流观点、互相探讨的过程。 在校内外的实践中，我参与过ESD不错P英语演讲赛事和GDP英文辩论赛事，并且都顺利获得了奖项。每一次备赛练习、上台展示和赛后复盘，都让我得到了很大的锻炼。我慢慢学会更加全面地看待问题，懂得从不同角度思考、理性分析，也让我在公众表达时更加自信、沉稳，临场反应也变得更加从容。 对我来说，演讲与辩论是一个很好的成长平台。在这里，我不仅可以大胆说出自己的观点，还能认识很多优秀的同龄人，在一次次思想的碰撞中拓宽自己的视野、提升自己的逻辑思维与思辨能力。 我的课余生活充实又丰富。我非常喜欢打排球，在团队运动中，我收获了满满的活力，也学会了团队配合、互相包容、坚持不放弃的精神。长期的运动，让我拥有更好的心态和抗压能力，做事也更加踏实、有毅力。 生活里，我十分喜欢猫咪。我喜欢小动物温柔治愈的陪伴，平时也会耐心细心地照顾它们。和小动物相处的时光，让我的性格变得更加细腻、温柔、懂得换位思考。 赛场之上，我敢于表达、善于思辨；生活之中，我热爱运动、心怀温柔。动静结合的日常，让我成为了一个阳光积极、思维清晰、待人真诚的学生。 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Valentina Ensink, en su charla “La vida que querés no se encuentra, se construye”, nos invita a detenernos y preguntarnos: ¿Las decisiones que tomamos realmente nacen de lo que queremos, o están influenciadas por lo que otros esperan de nosotros?
Vale nos propone reflexionar sobre nuestras elecciones, cuestionar los senderos que seguimos y recordar que tenemos el poder de elegir nuestro propio camino. Dejó la Facultad de Ingeniería a solo cinco materias de recibirse para dedicarse por completo al mundo digital. Ha ayudado a cientos de empresas a escalar su facturación mediante anuncios en línea, gestionando una inversión de más de 2.8 millones de dólares en publicidad para sus clientes. Actualmente lidera su propio equipo de media buying, con el que impulsa el crecimiento de negocios día a día.
Además, es fundadora de la Academia de Publicidad, una formación diseñada para aprender sobre anuncios desde cero. Esta iniciativa ya ha ayudado a más de 3000 personas en todo el mundo a genera
title: La vida que querés no se encuentra, se construye | Valentina Ensinck | TEDxPlaza Aberastain

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Pablo Montemurro, en su charla “El poder de editar nuestra propia historia”, nos invita a reflexionar sobre cómo las palabras y etiquetas que otros ponen sobre nosotros, así como las circunstancias difíciles que atravesamos, pueden llegar a convertirse en parte de la historia que creemos sobre quiénes somos.
Pero Pablo nos enseña que ni lo que otros dicen de nosotros ni las circunstancias que vivimos nos definen. Siempre tenemos la posibilidad de cuestionar esas historias, transformar aquello que nos limita y tomar el poder de editar y escribir nuestra propia historia. author: TEDx Talks
description:
How do we stay connected to a world that moves faster every day without losing ourselves in its current?
Costume designer and stylist Nikol Panagiotou reflects on the pressure to keep up with trends, social media and the constant demand to be visible. In a culture of endless scrolling and comparison, moving with the flow can gradually become conformity adopting tastes, choices and even ambitions before we have had the time to decide whether they truly belong to us.
Drawing from moments when she chose uncertainty over security and personal integrity over professional success, Nikol explores the power of a conscious “no.” For her, resisting the current does not mean rejecting change or the world around us. It means creating enough space to choose how we participate in it. Because the challenge is not simply to keep up with the flow, but to remain ourselves as the current changes.
